event-title.$: ENTRY INTO FORCE OF REQUEST FOR SUBSTANTIVE EXAMINATION

section.content: When a vehicle component is replaced, the estimation accuracy of the machine learning model used in the vehicle is lowered. The machine learning device is provided with: a learning unit (31) that learns a machine learning model used in the vehicle (1); and a detection unit (32) that detects replacement of a vehicle component mounted on the vehicle. When a vehicle component related to input data of a machine learning model is replaced, a learning unit performs relearning of the machine learning model using a training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component.
在车辆部件被进行了更换的情况下，在车辆中使用的机器学习模型的推定精度会降低。机器学习装置具备：学习部(31)，其进行在车辆(1)中使用的机器学习模型的学习；和检测部(32)，其对搭载于车辆的车辆部件的更换进行检测。学习部在与机器学习模型的输入数据有关的车辆部件被进行了更换的情况下，使用与更换后的车辆部件对应的训练数据集，进行机器学习模型的再学习。

Machine learning deviceTechnical Field

The present invention relates to a machine learning device.

Background

In recent years, with the progress of AI (artificial intelligence) technology, it has been studied to perform control using a machine learning model such as a neural network model in a vehicle. For example, in a machine learning system described in patent document 1, a neural network model is used to estimate the temperature of an exhaust gas purification catalyst provided in an internal combustion engine.

In order to improve the estimation accuracy of such a neural network model, it is necessary to learn the neural network model in advance. For example, as described in patent document 1, the server learns the neural network model, and the server transmits the learned neural network model to the vehicle.

Documents of the prior art

Patent document 1: japanese patent laid-open publication No. 2019-183698

Disclosure of Invention

Technical problem to be solved by the invention

When deterioration or failure of a vehicle component occurs along with use of a vehicle, replacement of the vehicle component is performed. In addition, in some cases, replacement of vehicle components is performed in order to mount higher-performance vehicle components on the vehicle.

However, machine learning models used in vehicles are typically matched to the characteristics of the vehicle components prior to replacement. Therefore, when the characteristics of the vehicle component change due to the replacement of the vehicle component, there is a risk that the estimation accuracy of the machine learning model is lowered.

In view of the above problems, an object of the present invention is to suppress a decrease in estimation accuracy of a machine learning model used in a vehicle when a vehicle component is replaced.

Means for solving the problems

The gist of the present disclosure is as follows.

(1) A machine learning device is provided with: a learning unit that learns a machine learning model used in a vehicle; and a detection unit that detects replacement of a vehicle component mounted on the vehicle, wherein when the vehicle component related to the input data of the machine learning model is replaced, the learning unit performs relearning of the machine learning model using a training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after the replacement.

(2) The machine learning device according to (1) above, wherein the learning unit performs relearning of the machine learning model using a training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after replacement only when the vehicle component relating to the input data of the machine learning model is replaced with a vehicle component having a different configuration.

(3) The machine learning device according to the above (1) or (2), further comprising an update unit that updates the machine learning model, wherein the learning unit is provided in a server, transmits a machine learning model that has been relearned to the vehicle, and the update unit applies the relearned machine learning model to the vehicle.

(4) The machine learning device according to the above (1) or (2), wherein the learning unit is provided in the vehicle, and applies the machine learning model that has been re-learned to the vehicle.

(5) The machine learning device according to any one of the above (1) to (4), wherein the machine learning model is a neural network model, and the learning unit updates parameters of the machine learning model set before relearning to relearn the machine learning model.

ADVANTAGEOUS EFFECTS OF INVENTION

According to the present invention, when a vehicle component is replaced, it is possible to suppress a decrease in estimation accuracy of a machine learning model used in a vehicle.

Detailed Description

Hereinafter, embodiments of the present invention will be described in detail with reference to the drawings. In the following description, the same reference numerals are assigned to the same components.

< first embodiment >

First, a first embodiment of the present invention will be described with reference to fig. 1 to 4. Fig. 1 is a diagram schematically showing the configuration of a vehicle 1 provided with a machine learning device according to a first embodiment of the present invention.

As shown in fig. 1, the vehicle 1 includes an actuator 11, a sensor 12, and an Electronic Control Unit (ECU) 20. That is, actuator 11, sensor 12, and ECU20 are mounted on vehicle 1. The actuator 11 and the sensor 12 are connected to the ECU20 so as to be able to communicate with each other via an in-vehicle Network conforming to the CAN (Controller Area Network) standard or the like.

The actuator 11 is an operating member required for running of the vehicle 1, and includes, for example, a member (an ignition plug, a fuel injection valve, a throttle valve drive actuator, an EGR control valve, and the like), a motor, a clutch, and the like required for operation of the internal combustion engine. The ECU20 controls the actuator 11.

The sensors 12 detect state quantities of the vehicle 1, the internal combustion engine, the battery, and the like, and include a vehicle speed sensor, a GPS receiver, an accelerator opening sensor, an air flow meter, an air-fuel ratio sensor, a crank angle sensor, a torque sensor, a voltage sensor, a temperature sensor, and the like. The output of the sensor 12 is sent to the ECU 20.

The actuator 11 and the sensor 12 constitute a vehicle component as a component mounted on the vehicle 1. In other words, the vehicle components include the actuator 11 and the sensor 12.

The ECU20 includes a communication interface 21, a memory 22, and a processor 23, and executes various controls of the vehicle 1. In the present embodiment, one ECU20 is provided, but a plurality of ECUs may be provided for each function.

The communication interface 21 has an interface circuit for connecting the ECU20 to an in-vehicle network conforming to CAN or the like. The ECU20 communicates with other in-vehicle devices as described above via the communication interface 21.

The memory 22 includes, for example, a volatile semiconductor memory (e.g., RAM) and a nonvolatile semiconductor memory (e.g., ROM). The memory 22 stores a program executed in the processor 23, various data used when various processes are executed by the processor 23, and the like.

The processor 23 has one or more CPUs (Central Processing units) and peripheral circuits thereof, and executes various processes. The processor 23 may further include an arithmetic circuit such as a logical operation unit or a numerical operation unit. The communication interface 21, the memory 22, and the processor 23 are connected to each other via signal lines.

In the present embodiment, the ECU20 functions as a machine learning device. Fig. 2 is a functional block diagram of the ECU20 of fig. 1. The ECU20 has a learning unit 31 and a detection unit 32. Learning unit 31 and detection unit 32 are functional blocks realized by processor 23 of ECU20 executing a program stored in memory 22 of ECU 20.

The learning unit 31 learns a machine learning model used in the vehicle 1. In the present embodiment, as the machine learning model, a neural network model that outputs at least one output data (also referred to as a target variable) from a plurality of input data (also referred to as explanatory variables) can be used.

First, an outline of the neural network model will be described with reference to fig. 3. Fig. 3 shows an example of a neural network model having a simple structure.

The circular symbols in fig. 3 represent artificial neurons. Artificial neurons are generally referred to as nodes or units (referred to as "nodes" in this specification). In fig. 3, L ═ 1 denotes an input layer, L ═ 2 and L ═ 3 denote hidden layers, and L ═ 4 denotes an output layer. Furthermore, the hidden layer is also referred to as an intermediate layer.

In FIG. 3, x1And x2Each node of the input layer (L ═ 1) and the output value therefrom are indicated, and y indicates the node of the output layer (L ═ 4) and the output value thereof. For example, in the nodes of the output layer, identity functions are used as activation functions. In this case, the total input value u calculated at the node of the output layer is directly output as the output value y from the node of the output layer.

The neural network model used in the vehicle 1 is stored in the memory 22 of the ECU20 or other storage device provided in the vehicle 1. The ECU20 causes the neural network model to output at least one value (output value) of output data by inputting a plurality of values (input values) of input data to the neural network model. In this case, as the value of each input data, for example, an output value of the sensor 12, a command value from the ECU20 to the actuator 11, a value calculated in the ECU20, or the like can be used.

The value of the output data output from the neural network model is used for the control of the vehicle 1. Further, the neural network model may be any one of a regression model and a classification model. When the neural network model is a regression model, the output data is, for example, the output torque Of the internal combustion engine, the concentration Of a predetermined component (HC, NOx, etc.) in the exhaust gas, the State Of Charge (SOC) Of the battery, and the like. On the other hand, in the case where the neural network model is a classification model, the output data is, for example, a result of abnormality determination of the predetermined sensor 12, a result of start determination of the internal combustion engine in the hybrid vehicle, and the like. The state quantities related to the output data are appropriately selected as input data.

In order to improve the accuracy of such a neural network model, it is necessary to learn the neural network model in advance. Therefore, the neural network model is learned in, for example, a production plant of a vehicle.

In the learning of the neural network model, a training data set is used which is composed of a combination of actual measurement values of a plurality of input data and actual measurement values (actual interpretation data or teacher data) of at least one output data corresponding to the actual measurement values. The actual measurement values of the input data and the output data are acquired using, for example, an engine mount, and the training data set is created by combining the corresponding actual measurement values.

In the learning of the neural network model, the parameters (the weight w and the bias b) of the neural network model are repeatedly updated by a known error back propagation method using a large number of training data sets so that the difference between the value of the output data output from the neural network model and the actually measured value of the output data becomes small. As a result, the neural network model is learned, and a learned neural network model is generated. The generated learned neural network model is mounted to ECU20 of vehicle 1 before shipment of vehicle 1. That is, the information of the learned neural network model (the structure of the model, the weight w, the offset b, and the like) is stored in the memory 22 provided in the ECU20 or in another storage device of the vehicle 1. After shipment of the vehicle 1, the learning unit 31 may learn the neural network model, and the learning unit 31 may generate the learned neural network model.

When deterioration or failure of a vehicle component such as the actuator 11 or the sensor 12 occurs along with use of the vehicle 1, replacement of the vehicle component is performed. In addition, in some cases, replacement of vehicle components is performed in order to mount higher-performance vehicle components on the vehicle 1.

However, the neural network model installed in the ECU20 matches the characteristics of the vehicle components before replacement. Therefore, when the characteristics of the vehicle component change due to the replacement of the vehicle component, there is a risk that the estimation accuracy of the neural network model is lowered. For example, in the case where a vehicle component is replaced with a vehicle component of a different structure, generally, the characteristics of the vehicle component may change. Even when a vehicle component is replaced with a vehicle component having the same structure, the characteristics of the vehicle component may vary depending on individual variations.

Thus, in the present embodiment, the detection unit 32 detects replacement of a vehicle component mounted on the vehicle 1. When a vehicle component related to input data of the neural network model is replaced, the learning unit 31 creates a training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component using the replaced vehicle component, and relearns the neural network model using the training data set. By relearning the neural network model in accordance with the replacement of the vehicle component in this way, it is possible to suppress a decrease in the estimation accuracy of the neural network model used in the vehicle 1 when the vehicle component is replaced.

The control described above will be described in detail below with reference to the flowchart of fig. 4. Fig. 4 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the relearning process in the first embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU20 at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S101, the detection unit 32 determines whether or not the replacement flag F is 1. The replacement flag F is set to 1 when the vehicle component is replaced, and the initial value of the replacement flag F is zero. If it is determined in step S101 that the replacement flag F is zero, the present control routine proceeds to step S102.

In step S102, the detection unit 32 determines whether or not a vehicle component related to input data of the neural network model has been replaced. For example, when the output value of the sensor 12 is used as input data of the neural network model, the sensor 12 corresponds to a vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model. In addition, when the command value from the ECU20 to the actuator 11 is used as input data of the neural network model, the actuator 11 corresponds to a vehicle component relating to the input data of the neural network model.

The detection unit 32 detects replacement of the vehicle component by reading identification information (model number, serial number, manufacturing number, and the like) of the vehicle component, for example. The detection unit 32 may detect replacement of a vehicle component by detecting an output waveform, an operating voltage, and the like of the vehicle component. The operator may input the replacement of the vehicle component to an input device (HMI or the like) of the vehicle 1, and the detection unit 32 may detect the replacement of the vehicle component based on the input to the input device.

If it is determined in step S102 that the vehicle component has not been replaced, the present control routine is ended. On the other hand, if it is determined in step S102 that the vehicle component has been replaced, the control routine proceeds to step S103. In step S103, the detection unit 32 sets the replacement flag F to 1.

Next, in step S104, the learning unit 31 creates a training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after replacement. In the training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after replacement, the output value of the vehicle component after replacement, the command value for the vehicle component after replacement, and the like are used as one of the actual measurement values of the input data. The vehicle 1 is provided with a sensor 12 and the like for acquiring an actual measurement value of output data of the neural network model. Therefore, the learning unit 31 can create a training data set by combining the corresponding measured values of the input data and the output data.

Next, in step S105, the learning unit 31 determines whether or not the number of training data sets corresponding to the vehicle component after replacement is equal to or greater than a predetermined value. The predetermined value is predetermined and set to the number required to obtain the required estimation accuracy of the neural network model. If it is determined in step S105 that the number of data sets for training is smaller than the predetermined value, the present control routine is ended. On the other hand, when it is determined in step S105 that the number of training data sets is equal to or greater than the predetermined value, the present control routine proceeds to step S106.

In step S106, the learning unit 31 performs learning (relearning) of the neural network model using the training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after the replacement. Specifically, the learning unit 31 repeatedly updates the parameters (the weight w and the offset b) of the neural network model by a known error back propagation method, and generates a relearned neural network model such that the difference between the value of the output data output from the neural network model and the actual measurement value of the output data is small.

For example, the initial values of the parameters (weight w and offset b) at the start of relearning are set to predetermined values. The initial value of the parameter at the time of start of the relearning may be a value set before the relearning, that is, a value obtained by learning the vehicle component before the replacement. In other words, the learning unit 31 may update the parameters of the neural network model set before the relearning to perform the relearning of the neural network model. Thus, the accuracy of estimating the neural network model can be efficiently improved by relearning, and the number of required training data sets can be reduced.

Next, in step S107, the learning unit 31 applies the relearned neural network model to the vehicle 1. In other words, the learning unit 31 updates the neural network model used in the vehicle 1. That is, the information of the neural network model stored in the memory 22 or other storage device of the ECU20 is rewritten. By using the re-learned neural network model in the vehicle 1, the value of the output data corresponding to the input data of the predetermined value can be estimated without detecting the actual value of the output data by the sensor 12 or the like.

Next, in step S108, the learning unit 31 sets the replacement flag F to zero. After step S108, the present control routine ends.

In addition, the characteristics of the vehicle component may vary greatly when the vehicle component is replaced with a vehicle component of a different structure. Therefore, the learning unit 31 may perform the relearning of the neural network model using the training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after the replacement only when the vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model is replaced with a vehicle component having a different structure. This can effectively suppress a decrease in the estimation accuracy of the neural network model, and reduce the amount of power consumption for relearning. In this case, in step S102, the detection unit 32 determines whether or not the vehicle component relating to the input data of the neural network model is replaced with a vehicle component having a different structure.

< second embodiment >

The configuration and control of the machine learning device according to the second embodiment are basically the same as those of the machine learning device according to the first embodiment except for the points described below. Therefore, the following description will focus on a second embodiment of the present invention, which is different from the first embodiment.

Fig. 5 is a schematic configuration diagram of a client server system 10 to which a machine learning apparatus according to a second embodiment of the present invention is applied. The client server system 10 includes a vehicle 1' and a server 4. The server 4 is capable of communicating with a plurality of vehicles including the vehicle 1'.

As shown in fig. 5, the server 4 is provided outside the vehicle 1', and includes a communication interface 41, a storage device 42, a memory 43, and a processor 44. The server 4 may further include an input device such as a keyboard and a mouse, an output device such as a display, and the like. The server 4 may be constituted by a plurality of computers.

The communication interface 41 is capable of communicating with the vehicle 1 ', and makes it possible for the server 4 to communicate with the vehicle 1'. Specifically, the communication interface 41 has an interface circuit for connecting the server 4 to the communication network 5. The server 4 communicates with the vehicle 1' via the communication interface 41, the communication network 5, and the wireless base station 6. The communication interface 41 is an example of a communication device.

The storage device 42 includes, for example, a Hard Disk Drive (HDD), a Solid State Drive (SSD), an optical recording medium, and the like. The storage device 42 stores various data, such as a computer program or the like for the processor 44 to execute various processes.

The memory 43 includes a semiconductor memory such as a Random Access Memory (RAM), for example. The memory 43 stores various data and the like used when the processor 44 executes various processes, for example.

The communication interface 41, the storage device 42, and the memory 43 are connected to the processor 44 via signal lines. The processor 44 has one or more CPUs and peripheral circuits thereof, and executes various processes. The processor 44 may further include an arithmetic circuit such as a logical operation unit or a numerical operation unit. Processor 44 is one example of a control device.

Fig. 6 is a view schematically showing a part of the configuration of the vehicle 1' of fig. 5. As shown in fig. 6, the vehicle 1' has a communication module 13 on the basis of the actuator 11, the sensor 12, and the ECU 20. The actuator 11, the sensor 12, and the communication module 13 are connected to the ECU20 so as to be able to communicate with each other via an in-vehicle network conforming to can (controller Area network) or other standards.

The communication module 13 is a device that enables communication of the vehicle 1 'with the outside of the vehicle 1'. The communication module 13 is, for example, a data communication module (dcm) capable of communicating with the communication network 5 via the wireless base station 6. In addition, as the communication module 13, a portable terminal (for example, a smartphone, a tablet terminal, a WiFi router, or the like) may be used. The communication module 13 is an example of a communication device.

In the second embodiment, the ECU20 functions as a part of the machine learning device. Fig. 7 is a functional block diagram of the ECU20 of fig. 6. The ECU20 has a detection unit 32 and an update unit 33. The detection unit 32 and the update unit 33 are functional blocks realized by the processor 23 of the ECU20 executing a program stored in the memory 22 of the ECU 20.

The detection unit 32 detects replacement of a vehicle component mounted on the vehicle 1, as in the first embodiment. The updating unit 33 updates the neural network model used in the vehicle 1'.

In the second embodiment, the learning of the neural network model used in the vehicle 1 'is performed in the server 4, and the learned neural network model is transmitted from the server 4 to the vehicle 1'. That is, the processor 44 of the server 4 functions as a learning unit that learns the neural network model used in the vehicle 1'.

When a vehicle component relating to input data of the neural network model is replaced, the processor 44 performs relearning of the neural network model using a training data set corresponding to the replaced vehicle component, and transmits the relearned neural network model to the vehicle 1'. When the relearned neural network model is received from the server 4, the update unit 33 of the vehicle 1 'applies the relearned neural network model to the vehicle 1'. By relearning the neural network model in accordance with the replacement of the vehicle component in this way, it is possible to suppress a decrease in the estimation accuracy of the neural network model used in the vehicle 1' when the vehicle component is replaced.

The control described above will be described in detail below with reference to flowcharts of fig. 8 and 9. Fig. 8 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the model update process in the second embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the ECU20 of the vehicle 1' at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S201, the detection unit 32 determines whether or not the replacement flag F is 1. The replacement flag F is set to 1 when the vehicle component is replaced, and the initial value of the replacement flag F is zero. If it is determined in step S201 that the replacement flag F is zero, the present control routine proceeds to step S202.

In step S202, the detection unit 32 determines whether or not a vehicle component relating to input data of the neural network model has been replaced, as in step S102 of fig. 4. In the case where it is determined that the vehicle component has not been replaced, the present control routine is ended. On the other hand, when it is determined that the vehicle component is replaced, the control routine proceeds to step S203.

In step S203, the detection unit 32 sets the replacement flag F to 1. After step S203, the present control routine proceeds to step S204. On the other hand, if it is determined in step S201 that the replacement flag F is 1, the present control routine skips steps S202 and S203 and proceeds to step S204.

In step S204, the update unit 33 creates a training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after replacement. In the training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after replacement, the output value of the vehicle component after replacement, the command value for the vehicle component after replacement, and the like are used as one of the actual measurement values of the input data. The vehicle 1' is provided with a sensor 12 for acquiring an actual measurement value of output data of the neural network model, and the like. Therefore, the updating unit 33 can create the training data set by combining the corresponding measured values of the input data and the output data.

Next, in step S205, the update unit 33 transmits the training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after the replacement to the server 4.

Next, in step S206, the update unit 33 determines whether or not the relearned neural network model is received from the server 4. If it is determined that the relearning completed neural network model has not been received, the control routine is terminated. On the other hand, when it is determined that the relearning completed neural network model is received, the present control routine proceeds to step S207.

In step S207, the updating unit 33 applies the relearned neural network model to the vehicle 1'. In other words, the updating unit 33 updates the neural network model used in the vehicle 1'. That is, the information of the neural network model stored in the memory 22 or other storage device of the ECU20 is rewritten.

Next, in step S208, the update unit 33 resets the replacement flag F to zero. After step S109, the present control routine ends.

Fig. 9 is a flowchart showing a control routine of the relearning process in the second embodiment of the present invention. The present control routine is repeatedly executed by the processor 44 of the server 4 at predetermined execution intervals.

First, in step S301, the processor 44 determines whether a training data set corresponding to a vehicle component after replacement is received from the vehicle 1'. If it is determined that the training data set has not been received, the control routine is terminated. On the other hand, in a case where it is determined that the training data set is received, the present control routine proceeds to step S302.

In step S302, processor 44 determines whether or not the number of training data sets corresponding to the vehicle component after replacement is equal to or greater than a predetermined value. The predetermined value is predetermined and set to the number required to obtain the required estimation accuracy of the neural network model. If it is determined in step S302 that the number of data sets is smaller than the predetermined value for training, the present control routine is ended. On the other hand, when it is determined in step S302 that the number of training data sets is equal to or greater than the predetermined value, the present control routine proceeds to step S303.

In step S303, the processor 44 performs learning (relearning) of the neural network model using the training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after replacement. Specifically, the processor 44 repeatedly updates the parameters (the weight w and the offset b) of the neural network model by a known error back propagation method to generate the relearned neural network model such that the difference between the value of the output data output from the neural network model and the actual measurement value of the output data becomes small.

For example, the initial values of the parameters (weight w and offset b) at the start of relearning are set to predetermined values. The initial value of the parameter at the time of start of the relearning may be a value set before the relearning, that is, a value obtained by learning the vehicle component before the replacement. In other words, the processor 44 may perform the relearning of the neural network model by updating the parameters of the neural network model set before the relearning. Thus, the accuracy of estimating the neural network model can be efficiently improved by relearning, and the number of required training data sets can be reduced.

Next, in step S304, the processor 44 transmits the relearned neural network model to the vehicle 1'. After step S304, the present control routine ends.

Further, a training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after replacement may be transmitted from a vehicle other than the vehicle 1' to the server 4. The training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after replacement may be created in the server 4 using an engine mount or the like.

In addition, as described above, the characteristics of the vehicle component may vary greatly when the vehicle component is replaced with a vehicle component of a different structure. Therefore, the processor 44 may perform the relearning of the neural network model using the training data set corresponding to the vehicle component after the replacement only when the vehicle component related to the input data of the neural network model is replaced with a vehicle component having a different structure. This can effectively suppress a decrease in the estimation accuracy of the neural network model, and reduce the amount of power consumption for relearning. In this case, in step S202, the detection unit 32 determines whether or not the vehicle component relating to the input data of the neural network model is replaced with a vehicle component having a different structure.

While the preferred embodiments of the present invention have been described above, the present invention is not limited to these embodiments, and various modifications and changes can be made within the scope of the claims. For example, the machine learning model used in the vehicle 1, 1' may be a machine learning model other than a neural network such as a random forest, a k-nearest neighbor method, or a support vector machine.
